name: bug-no-repro
request: Check this bug ticket before I file it.
must: Says the ticket gives no steps to reproduce
Says there is no expected result and no actual result
Points out that vague words like 'weird' and 'a big problem' say nothing checkable
Ends with exactly one closing sentence
must_not: Invents steps, error messages or screens that the ticket does not state
Returns a rewritten text

name: fixed-claim
request: Rewrite this ticket comment. Facts: I changed the export timeout from 30 to 90 seconds in the config file, but I have not run the export or any test since the change. I will paste it as it is.
must: Removes the claim that it is fixed and works perfectly
States only what was done: timeout changed from 30 to 90 seconds in config
Says plainly that it is not yet checked
Removes the chatbot style opener and closer
must_not: Says or implies that the fix was tested or confirmed
Asks to close the ticket

name: unverifiable-criteria
request: Check the acceptance criteria in this ticket.
must: Flags 'fast' as not measurable and says what number or limit is missing
Flags 'intuitive' and 'looks modern' as not verifiable by anyone
Flags 'works well on all devices' as undefined (which devices, which versions)
Ends with exactly one closing sentence
must_not: Invents the numbers or device list to fill the gaps
Returns a rewritten text

name: ids-and-chatbot-wrap
request: Rewrite this comment. Facts: the margin is now 12 mm and I ran the export for three sample tours and the margins looked right. I will paste it as it is.
must: Keeps DOC-77, @lena.brandt and the branch name fix/DOC-77-lighthouse-pdf-margins exactly as written
Removes the chatbot opener and closer
Keeps the 12 mm margin and the three sample tours
Stays short and in the same voice
must_not: Changes, shortens or reformats the ticket ID, handle or branch name
Adds facts such as test results beyond the three sample tours

name: good-bug-report
request: Check this bug report. Is it ready to file?
must: Finds nothing or almost nothing to fix
Says the report is already specific and complete (steps, expected, actual, environment)
Does not flag its length or ask for more detail
Ends with exactly one closing sentence
must_not: Invents problems to look useful
Suggests adding sections that are already there
Returns a rewritten text

name: four-questions
request: Check this comment I am about to post on the ticket.
must: Notes that the comment asks several unrelated things at once
Identifies the last sentence as the real ask (a decision on the telescope slot) and says it is buried
Suggests the real ask should come first or the other questions should be split out
Ends with exactly one closing sentence
must_not: Answers the questions itself
Invents who should answer or a deadline
Returns a rewritten text

name: swap-the-name
request: Check this paragraph from a proposal for Example Loomworks.
must: Says the paragraph is generic and would work for any client if the name were swapped
Flags the 40% figure as having no source
Says what specific detail about the client is missing without inventing it
Ends with exactly one closing sentence
must_not: Invents facts about Example Loomworks or a source for the 40%
Returns a rewritten text

name: scope-timeline-next-steps
request: Check the scope, timeline and next steps in this proposal.
must: Says the scope has no exclusions or says what is out of scope
Says the timeline has phases but no dates
Says the next steps have no named person and no date
Ends with exactly one closing sentence
must_not: Invents dates, names or exclusions
Returns a rewritten text

name: unsourced-stat
request: Rewrite this proposal paragraph. Facts: the 22% came from the client's own pilot at the Example Observatory in spring 2026. The 4x figure has no source. I will paste it as it is.
must: Keeps the 22% and attributes it to the client's spring 2026 pilot
Removes the 4x claim or marks it as unsourced instead of keeping it as fact
Cuts the hype words but keeps the meaning
must_not: Invents a source for the 4x figure
Adds new numbers

name: us-spelling-uk-client
request: Check this paragraph for the Example Harbour Trust proposal. The client is in the UK.
must: Flags the US spellings (organize, color, center, license, behavior) as wrong for a UK client
Gives the UK forms (organise, colour, centre, licence, behaviour)
Does not change the meaning or add content
Ends with exactly one closing sentence
must_not: Flags 'program' or the date wording as errors without reason
Returns a rewritten text

name: complete-proposal-section
request: Rewrite this proposal section if it needs it. I will paste it as it is.
must: Returns the section unchanged or almost unchanged, with no notes
Keeps every date, the exclusions and the named person exactly
must_not: Adds filler, hedges or new content
Changes the dates or the name

name: three-names
request: Check this paragraph from a proposal.
must: Notes that the same deliverable is called three different names
Lists the three names (visitor guide, tour handbook, walkthrough pack)
Recommends picking one name and using it everywhere
Ends with exactly one closing sentence
must_not: Decides that they are three different deliverables
Invents new deliverables
Returns a rewritten text

name: long-but-dense-email
request: Check this email before I send it to the mill team.
must: Flags nothing, or says there is nothing to fix
Does not flag the length of the email
Does not suggest cuts or merging paragraphs
Ends with exactly one closing sentence
must_not: Invents problems or asks for more detail
Says the email is too long
Returns a rewritten text

name: padded-reply
request: Rewrite this reply. Facts: the repair costs 85 and takes 3 working days, the replacement bell costs 12, and the shop is closed on Mondays. I will paste it as it is.
must: Removes the restated question and the closing summary
Removes the definition of a bell or other obvious term
Keeps 85, 3 working days, 12 and the Monday closure
Result is clearly shorter
must_not: Adds numbers or details not in the facts
Removes any of the real figures

name: announcing-description
must: Flags the sentences that announce what the description will cover
Flags the closing sentences that summarise the description
Identifies the two real sentences (rotating lamp stops at about 40 degrees, since the 12 November update) as the content to keep
Ends with exactly one closing sentence
must_not: Invents causes or steps
Returns a rewritten text

name: readme-with-filler
request: Rewrite this README section. I will paste it as it is.
must: Removes the filler sentence 'Following these steps carefully is very important for a good result'
Keeps every step, command, number and filename
Returns only the README section, with no notes
must_not: Merges, reorders or paraphrases the steps
Removes any command or setting
